items.hed: The Texans have four days to regroup before hosting the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night Football in Week 11, and the team's own injury report still carries both Woody Marks and David Montgomery as questionable coming out of Sunday's 27-24 collapse at Cleveland
items.insight: Houston's official schedule page confirms the short-week turnaround puts the Colts at Reliant Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 19, at 7:15 p.m. Central on Prime Video. The team's own injury report lists running backs Woody Marks (knee) and David Montgomery (groin) both as questionable, along with edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. (ankle) and guard Wyatt Teller (back/illness), as Houston tries to snap a stretch of four losses in five games and climb back from 3-6.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium, Houston, Feb. 5, 2017. Venue still.

items.hed: New Astros manager Brad Ausmus said at his introductory news conference that winning the World Series remains the only real goal every year, and his first task now is assembling a coaching staff, starting with a bench coach to replace Omar Lopez
items.insight: "Making the playoffs, great step. Winning the division, great step. But the goal is and should be, every single year, to win the World Series," Ausmus said at Daikin Park, according to MLB.com. The club has already declined to renew several assistant coaches, including catching instructor Tim Cossins and assistant pitching coach Ethan Katz, while retaining pitching coach Josh Miller, first-base coach Dave Clark and hitting coach Victor Rodriguez; Lopez remains with the organization in another role. Ausmus, a former Astros catcher and longtime friend of senior advisor Jeff Bagwell, said filling out the staff comes before any roster moves.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium, Houston, Feb. 5, 2017. Venue still (page hero shared across today's Texas desk; Astros are in their off-season).

items.hed: The Rockets play at the Miami Heat tonight at Kaseya Center, their first game since Sunday's 147-119 rout of Washington, with tipoff set for 6:30 p.m. Central
items.insight: The league's official game page lists tonight's matchup tipping off at 6:30 p.m. Central (7:30 p.m. Eastern) at Kaseya Center in Miami, continuing a stretch in which Houston has already beaten Golden State and Utah this month, according to NBA.com.
